holidays.name: National Watermelon Day
holidays.description: A day for slicing into the ultimate summer fruit. Picnics, fairs and backyard cookouts all get a juicy, seed-spitting centerpiece.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance. It celebrates one of the most popular treats of the American summer, and its origin is unclear.
holidays.funFact: Watermelon is about 92% water, so eating it on a hot August day really does help you cool down and hydrate.

holidays.name: National Grab Some Nuts Day
holidays.description: A day that rolls every nut into one celebration. Almonds, pistachios, pecans, peanuts and cashews are all invited, so grab a handful of your favorite.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It works as a catch-all for the many single-nut days spread through the calendar, such as National Almond Day and National Pecan Day.
holidays.funFact: Peanuts aren't true nuts. They're legumes that grow underground, which puts them in the same family as beans and lentils.
